S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).

subtypes.Animal Type: Marked fear of animals or insects like dogs, bees, snakes, or spiders.
subtypes.Natural Environment Type: Marked fear of the natural environment like storms, heights, water, or the dark.
subtypes.Blood-Injection-Injury Type: Marked fear of seeing blood, receiving injections, or medical procedures.
subtypes.Situational Type: Marked fear of specific situations like airplanes, elevators, tunnels, bridges, or enclosed spaces.
subtypes.Other Type: Marked fear of other situations like choking, vomiting, loud sounds, or costumed characters.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Anticipatory Anxiety: Strong anxiety triggered just by thinking about the possibility of encountering the phobic object.
subtypes.Immediate Panic Response: Overwhelming fear erupting immediately upon facing the phobic object.
subtypes.Physiological Panic Symptoms: Intense physical reactions such as heart palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, or trembling.
subtypes.Freezing: Feeling paralyzed or unable to move due to extreme fear.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.

subtypes.Active Avoidance: Intentionally and completely staying away from contact with the phobic object or situation.
subtypes.Functional Impairment due to Avoidance: Accepting severe restrictions on daily life, job, or social activities to avoid the phobic object.
subtypes.Enduring with Distress: Forcing oneself to endure the situation while experiencing intense fear and anxiety because it cannot be avoided.
subtypes.Reliance on Safety Signals: Barely enduring the exposure by relying on a companion or safety object.

symptom.disease_info: Specific phobia is characterized by marked, disproportionate fear or anxiety tied to a particular object or situation, with fear arising almost immediately on exposure and leading to avoidance or endurance with intense distress. The course may be persistent and impairing when the feared situation becomes hard to avoid in daily life; it is distinguished from broader anxiety conditions by its circumscribed focus rather than worry across many domains or fear of social evaluation.

patient.stressor: Keith’s difficulties began after repeated arguments with the shop owner, who insisted that every barber promote a new high-end straight-razor shave package and criticized Keith for being too cautious with blades. Across the following 11 months, the straight razor itself became the focus of a phobic fear: he could handle clippers and color work, but the razor station triggered immediate fear, and he started swapping clients, hiding the razors in drawers, or enduring the service only with intense anxiety. The avoidance became costly, leading to lost tips, complaints from regulars, and withdrawal from a regional barber battle where razor detailing was required. He eventually sought psychiatric care himself after realizing that his technical skill and livelihood were being organized around avoiding one tool.

S064.name: Phobic_Avoidance_Endure
S064.description: The phobic object or situation is actively avoided or endured with intense fear or anxiety.
S064.manifestation: I’m here because I’ve gotten to where I’ll do almost anything to avoid using the straight razor at work—switch clients, say the blade’s missing, hide it in the drawer—and if I can’t get out of it, I’m shaking through the whole shave.

S062.name: Specific_Phobic_Fear
S062.description: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation that is out of proportion to the actual danger. (Note: In children, may be expressed by crying, tantrums, freezing, or clinging).
S062.manifestation: I know it’s just a tool I trained with and I can use clippers all day, but when that straight razor is sitting open at my station it feels like I’m about to hurt somebody or cut myself badly.

S063.name: Immediate_Fear/Anxiety_Response
S063.description: The phobic object or situation almost always provokes immediate fear or anxiety.
S063.manifestation: The second I hear a client ask for the razor shave or I see the blade flipped open, my chest tightens, my hands get sweaty, and it’s like my body wants to back away before I even think.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve lost tips and had regular clients complain because I keep avoiding razor shaves or passing them off to other barbers, and I even backed out of a barber battle because razor detailing was required.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about 11 months, since the arguments with the shop owner over the straight-razor shave package started.
